100 beats (patterns); 8 chains of up to 99 links; optional memory expansion adds about 2.5x beat memory
Per voice: level fader, 3-position pan switch, tuning, individual output; 13th mixer channel is the programmable metronome
Tempo set by rotary dial and shown in BPM

Replaceable voice EPROMs for custom sounds
8-bit samples at about 28 kHz; stock voice clock rates roughly 12-30 kHz (vLinn)
Polyphony 10 voices (Rev 1) or 9 voices (Rev 2/3) for 12 sounds
No MIDI (pre-MIDI); Kenton MIDI retrofit kits exist

pack_contents: 13 mono 44.1 kHz 16-bit one-shots named by sound: 'LM1 Kick', 'LM1 Snare', 'LM1 Hat Cl', 'LM1 Hat Open', 'LM1 Cabasa', 'LM1 Tamb', 'LM1 Tom Hi', 'LM1 Tom Lo', 'LM1 Conga Hi', 'LM1 Conga Lo', 'LM1 Cowbell', 'LM1 Clave' (16 ms), 'LM1 Clap'. That is one file per stock voice, with the hat split into closed and open. No accent-level or tuned variants, no gaps, no loops. Subfolder 'MT-32' is unrelated: 30 Roland MT-32 rhythm samples plus MT32Drums.txt (made on an Akai S3000XL, 44.1 kHz 16-bit mono, dated 6 Oct 1998, no FX/EQ, not normalised, names of 12 characters or fewer). MT-32 sounds: agogo hi/lo, bongo hi/lo, cabasa, claves, conga hi/lo/muted hi, cowbell, crash, hand clap, closed hat, open hat 1 (3.7 s) and 2, kick, maracas, quijada, ride, rimshot, samba whistle long/short, acoustic and electronic snare, tambourine, timbale hi/lo, tom hi/mid/low. Measured: the LM1 clap, cowbell, cabasa, tambourine and kick appear to be the same recordings as the LinnDrum pack's Percussion/ and Bassdrums/ files.

pack_contents: 'Linn LinnDrum' has 52 one-shots in two sets. The first set is 24 mono files at the root named 'Linn<Sound><nn>': Kick01-02, Snare01-09, Hat_C/_O/_P, Tom01-02, Ride, Crash, Clap, Cowbell, Rimshot, Shaker, Tamborine, Ratchet. The second set is 28 stereo files in subfolders: Bassdrums/Bassdrum; Cymbals/Crash, Hat Closed-01..03, Hat Open, Ride; Percussion/Cabasa, Clap, Conga H/M/L -01/-02, Cowbell, Tambourine, Tom H-01/02, Tom L-01/02, Tom M-01; Snaredrums/Sidestick-01..03, 'Snarderum'-01..03 (sic). Numbered variants are probably tunings or alternates; 'Conga M', 'Ratchet', 'Shaker' and the '_P' hat are not stock LinnDrum voices. Measured duplicates: Bassdrum = LinnKick02 = LinnKick01, LinnSnare09 = Snarderum-02, LinnCowbell = Percussion/Cowbell, LinnTom01 = Tom L-01. 'Akai Linndrum' has 13 stereo files: Bassdrum, SD, Closed Hat, Open Hat, Ride, Crash (2.2 s), Clap, Cowbell, Tambourin, Shuffle, Tom H/M/L. Its kick, cowbell, clap, tambourine and 'Shuffle' (a cabasa) match the LinnDrum/LM-1 files at correlation 0.83-0.996, but play at a constant 0.90-0.96 of their speed. That points to Linn sounds transferred through a sampler at a different sample rate (inferred; the name suggests an Akai). Its crash, ride, open hat and toms match nothing in these packs. No loops anywhere.

pack_contents: 34 one-shots in two sets. 14 mono files named 'Linn 9000 <sound>': bell, cabasa, clap, conga, cowbell, crash, hat cl, hat open, kick, ride, snare, stick, tamb, tom. 20 stereo files with generic names: BAssdrum, Conga H/M/L, Cowbell-01/02, Crash-01..03, Hat Closed, Hat Open, Ping, Rim Shot, Snaredrum, Tambourine, Tom-01..05. pack_contents: 38 one-shots in two copies of the same set. 18 mono files 'DMX<Sound>': Kick01-02, Snare01-03, Hat_C, Hat_O, TomHi/Mid/Lo, TimbaleHi/Lo, Ride, Crash, Clap, Rim, Tamborine, Cabasa. 20 stereo files with generic names: Bassdrum-01..03, Snaredrum-01..03, Hat Closed, Hat Open, Tom H/M/L, Timbale H/M/L, Ride, Crash, Clap, Rim Shot, Tamborine, Cabasa. Every mono file has an identical stereo twin (correlation 1.000); the stereo set adds Bassdrum-03 and Timbale M. Snare 02/03 and Kick02/Bassdrum-03 are the same sample (probably level variants). No accented hi-hat file. Timbales and 'Cabasa' are not stock DMX sounds (stock has a shaker); probably optional chips. Tom H/M/L are three pitches of one tom. No loops.

accent: Programmable per sound: level 0-15 plus accent 0-15, added to the level with the sum capped at 15. The accented version is assigned to its own Drum Play button (A-D). Levels and accents are stored per segment and per song, so a song can carry its own mix, and they also apply at the individual outputs.
global_features: 12 sounds; 6 sound-select buttons with a PERC/DRUMS layer switch; 4 Drum Play buttons (A-D) each assignable to any sound or its accented version
Power-on Drum Play defaults: A = Bass, B = Snare, C = Cowbell, D = Ride
Auto Correct: 8, 8/3, 16, 16/3, 32, 32/3, or Hr (high resolution); default 8
Swing factor: 50, 54, 58, 63, 67 or 71%
36 segments (6 banks x 6) up to 99 measures; 8 songs up to 99 steps; repeats and tempo changes within songs
Tempo 40-240 BPM
Output jacks: BASS, SNARE/RIM, HATS, RIDE, CLAP, CLAVE/CWB, H/M TOMS, LO TOM, MIX OUT
No tuning or decay controls documented; no MIDI
Gate inputs A-D trigger the sounds on Drum Play buttons A-D; MET/TRIG output; clock in at 24 pulses per quarter note with a 1-99 divider (02 for LinnDrum 48 ppqn, 04 for DMX 96 ppqn); tape sync

RS-232 'External Computer Control' at 9600 baud. The low 4 bits pick the sound (0 Clave, 1 Cowbell, 2 Claps, 3 Open Hi Hat, 4 Closed Hi Hat, 5 Ride, 6 Bass, 7 Snare, 8 Rimshot, 9 HiTom, A MidTom, B LowTom, C Metronome) and the high 4 bits the level
Samples recorded at Ayre Studios, San Jose; drums played by Bill Gibson and Chris Pedersen; design by Dave Rossum

pack_contents: 39 one-shots in two sets. 12 stereo files with generic names cover all 12 stock sounds: Bassdrum, Snaredrum, Rim Shot, Tom H/M/L, Claves, Cowbell, Clap, Hat Closed, Hat Open, Cymbal (the ride). 27 mono files named 'Drumulator<Sound>': Kick01-02, Snare01-04, Hat_C/_O/_P, Tom02, Tom03, ETomHi/Mid/Lo, Ride, Crash, Clap, Clave, Cabasa, Conga01-02, AgogoHi/Lo, Block, Tamborine, TimbHi/Lo. The mono set includes many non-stock sounds (agogo, block, cabasa, congas, crash, electronic toms, timbales, tambourine); these are probably alternate sound chips (inferred). Measured duplicates: DrumulatorSnare03 = Snaredrum, DrumulatorTom02 = Tom M, DrumulatorClap ~ Clap, DrumulatorKick01 ~ Bassdrum. No loops.

accent: Velocity-sensitive pads (piezo sensor) and MIDI note triggers. Accent levels for programming were not documented in the sources found.

built_in_effects.notes: SSM2044, 4-pole, time-varying (CCRMA). Hard-wired to those channels. Channels 3-6 probably have fixed low-pass filters and 7-8 none, as on the SP-1200 (inferred, unverified for the SP-12).

global_features: 8 velocity pads, 8 sliders, 8-voice polyphony, 8 individual outputs plus mix
4 banks give 32 sound slots (SP-1200 description; the SP-12 article says up to 32 user samples)
24 ROM sounds plus user sampling; the standard unit is about 1.2 s (CCRMA spec list; other figures of 2.2-2.5 s exist) and the Turbo 5 s
12-bit; sample rate 27.5 kHz (r-massive, CCRMA) vs 26.04 kHz (Wikipedia), a conflict
No reconstruction filter (Wikipedia)
Sample editing: truncate, decay, detune
Swing and quantize present; values not found
100 patterns and 100 songs (400 each with the Turbo upgrade)
MIDI note triggers in/out; sync to MIDI, SMPTE and analog click; cassette and Commodore 1541 storage
Shown as 'Drumulator II' in Feb 1985; replaced by the SP-1200 in Aug 1987

sound_bank.list_source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E-mu_SP-12 (categories). ROM chips per https://zine.r-massive.com/?p=5771: MS1 Electric Snare, Rimshot, Cowbell, Tom; MS2 Bass/Kick, Electric Tom, Hi-Hat, Clap; MS3 Ride, Snare; MS4 Crash. Toms are one sound transposed.

pack_contents: 68 stereo 44.1 kHz 16-bit one-shots in folders, numbered rather than named. BASSDRUM: Bassdrum-01..14. SNARES: Snaredrum-01..21 and Rim Shot-01..02. Toms: Tom H-01..06, Tom L-01..06, Tom M-01, -02, -03, -05 (M-04 missing). Cymbals: Crash, Hat Closed-01/02, Hhopen1, Ride. Percussion: Blow1, Clap, Cowbell. Misc: Metal-01..03, Scratch, Shot-01..03. Measured duplicates: Snaredrum-01 = Snaredrum-19, Bassdrum-07 = Bassdrum-12; near-duplicates 11~21 and 10~20 (snares). Far more than the 24 ROM sounds, so most are user samples. No loops.

global_features: Hand-built modular synthesizer; customers chose modules from a list (e.g. Quad Inverter, Sample-and-Hold, Dual Reverb)
Designed by Dave Rossum and Scott Wedge; production from 1972 per the History section ('built in 1974' per the lead)
Microprocessor-controlled polyphonic keyboard and sequencer, claimed by E-mu as a first and patented

No fixed drum voices. Drums would be patched (inferred, no source): kick from a sine or triangle oscillator or self-oscillating filter with a fast pitch envelope into a short VCA envelope; snare and hats from noise through band- or high-pass filters with short envelopes; toms from an oscillator with a pitch drop; triggered by sequencer gates
pack_contents: 5 stereo 44.1 kHz 16-bit synthesized one-shots: Bassdrum-01 (0.90 s), Bassdrum-02 (0.74 s), EmuPong (0.15 s), Flick01 (0.12 s), Flick-02 (0.055 s). Names are inconsistent (Flick01 vs Flick-02). No patch documentation, no loops.
